comments.author: Jeffrey Lai
comments.text:
Hi Product Hunt! 👋 I’m Jeffrey, building IrisGo.  
We’re launching an offering for solopreneurs and small business owners who juggle multiple roles, and spend too much time on recurring admin tasks.  
[https://irisgo.ai/solopreneur](https://irisgo.ai/solopreneur)  
If you’re spending hours each week managing your inbox, tracking priorities, summarizing meetings, preparing briefs, and filing expenses, you know it’s time that could be spent on customers and growth.
IrisGo learns these workflows by watching how you work, then automates them on your device. No repeated prompts, and your sensitive data stays on your device. Our **Watch & Learn** feature is central to understanding how you work, and handling that task forever.   
We’d love to learn:
*   Which of these tasks takes the most time in your day?
*   Was it clear on how to get started?
*   Where would you want more control or explanation?
Try the demo and let us know what works—or where you get stuck. We’ll be here to answer questions and learn from your feedback.
[https://irisgo.ai/solopreneur](https://irisgo.ai/solopreneur)

comments.text:
Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I'm Rick, co-founder of Alkera, building Databench with Andrew Tran and Tony Li. Before starting Alkera, we worked closely with data teams at places including TikTok, Ramp, and Hudson River Trading.  
Alkera provides a unified platform for data engineering, data science, and data analytics work. We've noticed a significant need for an agent-native data science solution beyond traditional Jupyter notebooks.  
**❌ The Problem**
While new agent-native interfaces such as ADEs have significantly increased software engineers' productivity, data teams are still stuck with the traditional Jupyter notebook, with little evolution or adaptation for agent-first, collaborative workflows. Another problem with agentic work for data is the lack of accountability, traceability, and reproducibility, which makes it hard to verify and reproduce agent-generated work.
This is why we built Databench, the **_open-source_** multiplayer workspace for data science, analytics, and engineering. Work alongside teammates and agents in notebooks and chats and run any cell or agent on your laptop or a remote computing node.  
**✅ What Databench provides:**
*   **Open-source subset of the Alkera product** licensed under Apache 2.0
*   **Multiplayer SQL and Python notebooks** that you share live with teammates and agents
*   **Connection to databases** that are SQLAlchemy compatible (PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL, and many more)
*   **Reactive notebooks** based on marimo that rerun stale cells based on changes to SQL & Python
*   **Fully web-based** with rich file editors and notebook editing
*   **Live collaboration** with live cursors and edits from teammates and agents
*   **Run chats and notebooks anywhere:** your laptop, a remote compute node, or a GPU cluster
*   **Declarative charting library** for pretty graphs every time in your notebooks  
Try it free at [https://alkera.ai](https://alkera.ai/) or self-host from GitHub: [https://github.com/AlkeraAI/Databench](https://github.com/AlkeraAI/Databench)  
If you have any questions or concerns, the team will be online all day to help!

comments.author: Aiden Lee
comments.text:
Hi everyone, I'm Aiden, co-founder and CTO at TwelveLabs. Excited to share Pegasus 1.6 with you today.
Every robotics and physical AI team we talk to is sitting on the same problem: hours of first-person footage that's the raw material for action labeling and next-action prediction, and no foundation model actually built to understand it. General-purpose video models are trained on broadcast and third-person footage. Point them at a wearable or a robot's own camera and they miss what's actually happening.
Pegasus 1.6 is our answer. It's the first TwelveLabs model built for egocentric (first-person) video understanding. Pegasus 1.6 expands on Pegasus 1.5's Time-Based Metadata (TBM), which extracts timestamped, structured metadata from custom schemas, by adding support for egocentric video and task narration. We've also sharpened detailed recognition of hand, tool, and object interactions , while speeding up processing for high-volume video workloads. 
As an update to 1.5’s capabilities, we also have improved performance on in-depth metadata extraction and on grounded entity recognition, the ability to name a character based on context clues in the video.  
Concretely, for robotics and data teams that means: point Pegasus at raw egocentric clips  and get back structured action labels, compliance ratings, and timestamps you can use directly in a training pipeline instead of a manual labeling pass that costs $4–$22/hour of footage.
Physical AI is a new domain for us, so if you're working with egocentric (human or teleoperated) data and hit edge cases, I want to hear about them. Thanks!
comments.kr:
여러분 안녕하세요, TwelveLabs의 공동 창업자이자 CTO인 Aiden입니다. 오늘 Pegasus 1.6을 여러분께 선보이게 되어 매우 기쁩니다.

저희가 만난 모든 로보틱스 및 Physical AI 팀은 똑같은 문제에 직면해 있었습니다. 바로 행동 라벨링과 다음 행동 예측의 원천이 되는 수천 시간의 1인칭(Egocentric) 영상 데이터를 보유하고 있으면서도, 이를 진정으로 이해할 수 있는 파운데이션 모델이 전무하다는 점이었습니다. 기존의 범용 비디오 모델들은 방송이나 3인칭 시점 영상으로 학습되어, 웨어러블 카메라나 로봇 자체 카메라에 적용하면 실제로 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지 핵심을 놓치고 맙니다.

Pegasus 1.6은 이에 대한 저희의 해답입니다. 1인칭 비디오 이해를 위해 특화 설계된 최초의 TwelveLabs 모델입니다. 커스텀 스키마로부터 타임스탬프가 포함된 구조화 메타데이터를 추출하는 시간 기반 메타데이터(TBM) 기능을 확장하여, 1인칭 시점 비디오 및 작업 내레이션 생성을 전면 지원합니다. 또한 손과 도구, 객체 간의 정밀한 상호작용 인식을 대폭 향상시켰으며 고용량 비디오 워크로드 처리를 위한 속도도 크게 개선했습니다.

구체적으로 로보틱스 및 데이터 팀에게 이는 다음과 같은 의미를 갖습니다: 원시 1인칭 영상을 Pegasus에 입력하기만 하면, 영상 1시간당 $4~$22의 비용이 들던 번거로운 수작업 라벨링 없이도 훈련 파이프라인에 즉시 투입 가능한 구조화된 행동 라벨, 컴플라이언스 평가, 타임스탬프를 곧바로 확보할 수 있습니다.

Physical AI는 저희에게도 새로운 개척 분야이므로, 1인칭 데이터를 다루시면서 발견하는 특이 케이스나 의견이 있다면 언제든 편하게 들려주세요. 감사합니다!
